## Project instructions (AGENTS.md — workbench default)

# AGENTS.md — workbench default

> Instructions for any agent working through the Ember Workbench. This is the
> **fallback**: a workspace with its own `AGENTS.md` at its root overrides this
> file entirely. Put project-specific rules there, not here.
>
> Keep this short. It is re-sent on every turn and competes with the work for
> context. Truncated at 8,000 chars.

## Before you touch anything

1. **Read before you write.** Never edit a file you have not read this session.
   Never claim an action you did not take — the operator sees your report, not
   your tools.
2. **Look for the project's own rules.** If the workspace has `AGENTS.md`,
   `CLAUDE.md`, or a `README.md` with conventions, they outrank this file.
3. **Check for a skill.** `use_skill` lists what is available. A stored
   procedure beats improvising, and router skills route to sub-files — load
   those with `use_skill name="..." file="..."`.

## While you work

- **Small steps, but finish.** One logical action at a time, and keep going
  until the task is actually done. Stopping at the first plausible-looking
  result is the most common failure here.
- **Minimal diffs.** `edit_file` over `write_file`; match the surrounding code's
  style, naming, and comment density rather than importing your own.
- **Commands need approval** unless the session is in Auto mode. If one is
  denied, change the approach — do not retry the identical call.
- **Long output is clipped in the middle**, keeping the head and the tail.
  Build errors live in the tail; read it.

## Dependencies — do not churn them

**Do not edit `package.json` (or the equivalent manifest) to change versions
that are already there.** Pinned versions are pinned deliberately: someone chose
them, and a toolchain that shifts under a project turns every later result into
a comparison of library versions rather than of the work.

The single exception: if the task genuinely needs a package that is **not
listed**, add that package. Add it — do not rewrite the versions of the ones
around it.

- If a lockfile exists, install with `npm ci`, not `npm install`. `ci` installs
  exactly what the lockfile says; `install` is free to resolve something newer
  and silently rewrite the lockfile.
- If a pinned version genuinely blocks the task, **say so and stop**. Do not
  downgrade your way around it. That is a decision for the operator, and it is
  usually a sign the real problem is elsewhere.
- Never delete or regenerate a lockfile to make an error go away.

## Before you say you are done

- **Run it.** If what you built can be built, tested, or opened, do that. Read
  the output. Fix what breaks. Repeat until it is clean.
- **Never report completion on code you have not executed.** If you could not
  run it, say so plainly and say why — that is a fine answer; a false "done"
  is not.
- **Report what changed and what you verified.** No preamble, no flattery, no
  summary of how hard the task was.

## Memory

Use `remember` when something is worth carrying past this turn:

- `lesson` — something that cost you time and would cost the next agent time
  (a build quirk, a wrong assumption, an API that does not behave as documented).
- `decision` — a choice made and its reason, so it is not silently relitigated.

Memory is per-workspace and is injected into future sessions on this workspace.
Record the *finding*, not the narration. One line each.

## The working method — CRAFT.md

`CRAFT.md` at the workbench root is the long-form method: how to read what is
actually being asked, how to split a problem along verification seams, how to
know when you are guessing. It is **not** injected by default — roughly 4k
tokens on every turn.

Set `EMBER_CRAFT=on` to load it into the system prompt when the work is hard,
unfamiliar, or high-stakes enough to be worth the budget.

The shipped copy is deliberately generic. If you keep your own working-method
document — one that names your projects, your conventions, and the specific
mistakes that have actually cost you time — point `EMBER_CRAFT_PATH` at it
instead. A method doc is worth more when its examples are yours.

## Honesty rules

- Say "I do not know" rather than producing a confident guess.
- Distinguish what you verified from what you assume. Mark assumptions.
- If a constraint blocks the literal request, say so **before** substituting
  something else — not in the delivery summary.
- Surface bad news early. A problem reported at step two is cheap; the same
  problem discovered at step ten is not.

---

## Environment

- **Platform:** Windows (win32)
- **Workspace root:** `C:/Data/AI/Projects/LMStudioComparison/Results/_v2-shakedown-2026-09-07/local`  — every path you pass to a file tool is relative to this, and paths outside it are rejected.
- **run_command shell:** git-bash — POSIX sh, *not* cmd.exe or PowerShell. use Unix syntax (`ls`, `rm`, `cat`, `grep`, `/dev/null`, forward slashes, `$VAR`, `&&`). cmd.exe builtins are NOT available and fail in confusing ways: `dir`, `type`, `findstr`, `%VAR%`, and especially `2>nul`, which silently creates a FILE named `nul` instead of discarding output — write `2>/dev/null`.
- **Working directory does not persist** between commands. Each one starts at the workspace root.

---

## This session: coding agent

You operate on files inside one workspace via tools.
Rules, in order:
1. Never invent file contents — read before you edit. Never claim an action you did not take.
2. Plan briefly (one or two sentences), then act with tools. Work in small steps, but keep going until the task is actually done — do not stop at the first plausible-looking result.
3. Prefer minimal diffs via edit_file; write_file only for new files. Match the existing code style and document public APIs the way the surrounding code does.
4. Writes and commands need user approval; if denied, adjust your approach rather than retrying the same call.
5. Verify your own work before reporting it done. If what you built can be run — a build, a test suite, a page — run it, read the output, and fix what breaks. Never report completion on code you have not executed. If you could not run it, say so plainly and say why.
6. Be terse. Report what changed and what you verified, not how hard you worked. No flattery, no filler.

Skills — stored procedures under .claude/skills in this workspace. When a task matches one, call use_skill with its name BEFORE improvising, then follow the returned instructions:
- context7-mcp: Fetch up-to-date library and framework documentation via Context7. Use when the user asks about API usage, configuration, version migration, or setup for any library, framework, SDK, or CLI tool.
- create-second-brain-prd: 
- domain-modeling: Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when discussing codebase terminology, writing or editing a CONTEXT.md, or recording or editing an ADR.
- gauntlet-loop: Turns any goal into one short, paste-ready "gauntlet loop" prompt - a prompt that makes an agent set a concrete quality bar, split the work into small judgeable pieces, run a builder and a separate ha
- goal-prep: Goal Prep for GoalBuddy. Use for broad, long-running, stalled, vague, detailed, planned, or unhealthy Codex or Claude Code work that needs a structured /goal intake, autonomous task discovery, role-ta
- grill-me: A relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design.
- grilling: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.
- openai-game-studio: 
- playwright-cli: Automates browser interactions for web testing, form filling, screenshots, and data extraction. Use when the user needs to navigate websites, interact with web pages, fill forms, take screenshots, tes
- playwright-mcp: Browser automation via Playwright MCP (navigate, click, fill, screenshot, extract content). Use when the user needs to interact with web pages, test UIs, extract data, or verify deployments in a real 
- prototype: Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question. Use when the user wants to sanity-check whether a state model or logic feels right, or explore what a UI should look like.
- research: Investigate a question against high-trust primary sources and capture the findings as a Markdown file in the repo. Use when the user wants a topic researched, docs or API facts gathered, or reading le
- stitch: Work with Google Stitch AI design platform. Use when the user wants to generate UI screens, manage design systems, create projects, edit screens, or export designs to code.
- to-spec: "Turn the current conversation into a spec and publish it to the project issue tracker: no interview, just synthesis of what you've already discussed."
- unity-cli: Use when interacting with Unity CLI from the terminal, or to control a running/connected Unity Editor from the command line — create or modify GameObjects, edit scenes and assets, inspect the hierarch
- wayfinder: Plan a huge chunk of work (more than one agent session can hold) as a shared map of decision tickets committed to the repo, and resolve them one at a time until the way to the destination is clear.

[Earlier turns were compacted to save context. Summary of the work so far:]

**Hand-off note — Space_Invaders implementation**

**Task / scope**
- Build exactly one game: `Space_Invaders/`.
- Do not implement any other game from the collection.
- Approved plan exists at `Space_Invaders/plan.md`.
- Stack: Vite 5.4.19, `three@0.160.1`, vanilla ES modules, no physics libraries, 100% procedural assets, `MeshStandardMaterial`, glassmorphism UI, keyboard + gamepad input, object pooling, 500-particle cap, explicit `.dispose()` cleanup.

**Files created / changed**
Root:
- `package.json`
- `vite.config.js`
- `.gitignore`

Shared layer:
- `shared/utils/Math.js`
- `shared/utils/Noise.js`

- `Space_Invaders/UFO.js`

- `Space_Invaders/Arena.js`
- `Space_Invaders/UI.js`

**Key architecture decisions**
- Dependency direction is strictly: `Space_Invaders → shared → three`.
- Shared VFX are centralized in `shared/core/`:
  - `ParticleManager`: one `InstancedMesh`, hard cap 500, priority-based spawn rejection.
  - `Shockwave`: pooled emissive rings.
  - `MotionTrail`: fading ribbon trail.
  - `FloatingText`: DOM-based projected score popups.
  - `HitStop`: timescale dilation.
  - `CameraShake`: trauma-based shake.
  - `Audio`: WebAudio synthesized SFX + music.
- Vite is multi-page; final `vite.config.js` must avoid `import.meta.url` because it broke in the bundled config.
- PostFX stack: `EffectComposer` + `RenderPass` + `UnrealBloomPass` + custom shader pass + `OutputPass`.
- Game-specific entities use hand-written kinematics and collision logic; no external physics.

**Errors already hit and fixed**
1. **Vite config failure**
   - Error: `TypeError: Invalid URL` from `vite.config.js`.
   - Cause: use of `import.meta.url` in Vite’s bundled config.
   - Fix: rewrote `vite.config.js` using plain relative paths.

2. **`CameraShake.js` build failure**
   - Error: `Identifier "t" has already been declared`.
   - Fix: renamed conflicting local/parameter.
   - Follow-up issue: a later edit accidentally left `this.time` uninitialized.
   - Fix: restored `this.time` initialization in the constructor.

3. **Missing core modules**
   - Build failed because `shared/core/Engine.js` and `shared/core/Input.js` were not actually on disk.
   - Fix: wrote both files.

4. **`main.js` API mismatches**
   - After writing `Input.js`, `main.js` had two API mismatches.
   - Fix: edited `main.js` to match the real `Input` / bootstrap APIs.

5. **Three addon path check**
   - A check for `three/package.json` failed due to package exports restrictions.
   - Verified needed addon paths exist:
     - `three/addons/postprocessing/EffectComposer.js`
     - `three/addons/postprocessing/RenderPass.js`
     - `three/addons/postprocessing/UnrealBloomPass.js`
     - `three/addons/postprocessing/OutputPass.js`
     - `three/addons/utils/BufferGeometryUtils.js`

**Current blocker**
- The build has **not yet been re-run successfully** after `Engine.js` and `Input.js` were added.
- More importantly, there is a **systemic API mismatch** between `Game.js` and the actual entity modules.
- `Game.js` was written against an idealized interface, but the real modules use different constructor signatures and method names.

**Known bad / unverified calls in `Game.js`**
- `player.powerups`
- `formation.hitAt`
- `formation.forEachAlive`
- `player.explode`
- `player.invulnerable`

These do **not** match the observed real APIs.

**Observed real constructor signatures**
- `new Player(scene, input, fx)`
- `new Barricade(scene, { centers, topY, cell, cols, rows, hp })`
- `new Bullet(scene, geometry, material, trailColor, halfX, halfY)`
  - has `fire(x, y, vx, vy)`
- `new UFO(scene, fx)`
- `new PowerUp(scene, { fallSpeed, killY })`
- `new ParticleManager(scene, { max })`
- `new Shockwave(scene, { max, z })`
- `new FloatingText({ container, camera, max })`
- `new HitStop()`
- `new MotionTrail({ segments, width, color, intensity })`
- `new Audio()`

**Immediate next steps**
1. Read the full current contents of:
   - `Space_Invaders/Game.js`
   - `Space_Invaders/main.js`
   - `Space_Invaders/Player.js`
   - `Space_Invaders/InvaderFormation.js`
   - `Space_Invaders/Barricade.js`
   - `Space_Invaders/Bullets.js`
   - `Space_Invaders/UFO.js`
   - `Space_Invaders/PowerUp.js`
   - `Space_Invaders/Arena.js`
   - `Space_Invaders/UI.js`
   - all `shared/core/*` modules
2. Build an exact API map:
   - exported class names
   - constructor signatures
   - public methods
   - expected update/hit/fire/spawn/trigger signatures
3. Rewrite `Game.js` to use the **actual** entity APIs.
   - Preserve the intended game logic:
     - state machine
     - player movement/firing
     - invader formation stepping
     - collisions
     - scoring
     - lives/waves
     - UFO
     - power-ups
     - VFX routing
     - audio hooks
4. Re-check `main.js` against the real shared APIs.
5. Ensure every import resolves to a real export.
6. Ensure every method called on an imported object actually exists.
7. Run the production build:
   - `npx vite build`
   - or `npm run build` if the script exists
8. After build passes, verify the game is actually playable:
   - launch Vite dev/preview
   - confirm no console errors
   - confirm input works
   - confirm core loop reaches win/loss

**Definition of done**
- `vite build` passes.
- No unresolved imports.
- No missing methods.
- Game launches and is playable.
- Core loop works through to win or loss.
- No placeholder code.
- No unimplemented stubs.

**Most important current state**
- The project is close, but **not yet build-verified**.
- The biggest risk is not missing files anymore; it is **API inconsistency between `Game.js` and the real entity/shared modules**.
- The next productive action is to reconcile `Game.js` to the actual APIs, then rebuild.

## What I reconciled and fixed

The hand-off flagged API mismatches in `Game.js`, but the real problems were broader. After reading every file and building the exact API map, I fixed:

**Bootstrap (`main.js` / `index.html`)**
- `getElementById('game-root')` → `#app` (the actual container)
- `new Arena(scene)` → `new Arena(scene, textures)` — Arena requires a `ProceduralTextures` instance
- `new Game({ engine, … })` → `new Game({ scene, … })` — Game reads `scene`, not `engine`
- Removed the dead `fx.trail` (Bullets build their own trails) and added the missing `arena.update(realDt)` (starfield + light-flash decay were never running)
- Rewrote `index.html`: the static HUD/screens used CSS class names that didn't match UI.js's generated markup at all, and the duplicate `id="hud"` broke the UI root. Now the CSS matches UI.js exactly and the dead static DOM is gone.

**Game logic (`Game.js`)**
- Menu never showed on load — constructor set `state='menu'` but never called `_setState('menu')`
- SHIELD power-up was dead — `player.hit()` (the shield absorb) was never called
- UFO never appeared — `ufo.launch()` was never triggered; added a per-wave spawn timer
- Victory state was unreachable — `MAX_WAVE` was defined but unused; wired the wave-10 → victory path

**Entity bugs**
- `Bullets.js` called `trail.reset()` — `MotionTrail` has `clear()`, not `reset()` (threw on every shot)
- `PowerUp.testCollect` returned a pickup whose type had already been reset to `'RAPID'` by the pool's release hook — so a BOMB pickup applied RAPID. Now snapshots fields before release.
- `Player.wide` was never initialized in the constructor

**Shared (`Input.js`)**
- `update()` cleared the edge-press set every frame, wiping keyboard presses that fired between frames — fast pause/start toggles silently failed. Now edges are computed as held-now vs held-last-frame.

- Menu → LAUNCH → playing; HUD score/wave/lives correct
- Fire, move, pause/resume all work
- **Loss path**: 3 deaths → "EARTH FALLEN" game-over → RETRY restarts (reached in ~14s of real play)
- **Win path**: wave-10 clear → "GALAXY SECURED" victory → PLAY AGAIN resets to wave 1
- BOMB clears enemy bullets; SHIELD sets `player.shield`; UFO kill scores + deactivates
- Production build (`vite preview`) loads and plays identically
- `vite build` clean (39 modules), no unresolved imports, no missing methods, no stubs/placeholders

**Vite strategy.** One project at the root, multi-page: `vite.config.js` lists each game's `index.html` as a build input, so every game is an isolated entry with its own bundle. Games import the shared layer via relative paths (`../../shared/core/Engine.js`); Three.js addons resolve through the package's exports map (`three/addons/postprocessing/EffectComposer.js`). Dependency direction is strictly one-way: `game → shared → three`. No game ever imports another game; nothing in `shared/` knows a game exists.

**Shared-utilities strategy.** The six required VFX (shake, particles, hit-stop, trails, shockwaves, floating text) live *only* in `shared/core/` and are composed by every game — so the next game in the collection gets all of them for free. `ParticleManager` is the single allocation point for particles (one `InstancedMesh`, 500-instance hard cap enforced by the manager, not by callers). `ObjectPool` is generic so each game pools its own entities (balls, bricks, enemies) with zero per-frame allocation. `Engine.dispose()` guarantees teardown: it walks the scene graph and calls `.dispose()` on every geometry, material, and texture, and the texture factory keeps a registry so canvas textures are freed exactly once.

Let me write the sprite mask builder:

```js
function buildSpriteGeometry(mask, width, height, depth) {
  const cols = mask[0].length;
  const rows = mask.length;
  const px = width / cols;
  const py = height / rows;
  const boxes = [];
  for (let r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
    for (let c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
      if (mask[r][c] === '#') {
        const box = new THREE.BoxGeometry(px * 0.92, py * 0.92, depth);
        const x = (c - (cols - 1) / 2) * px;
        const y = ((rows - 1) / 2 - r) * py;
        box.translate(x, y, 0);
        boxes.push(box);
      }
    }
  }
  const merged = mergeGeometries(boxes);
  boxes.forEach(b => b.dispose());
  return merged;
}
```

- PostFX stack: `EffectComposer` + `RenderPass` + `UnrealBloomPass` + custom shader pass + `OutputPass`.
- Game-specific entities use hand-written kinematics and collision logic; no external physics.

   - Fix: wrote both files.

   - After writing `Input.js`, `main.js` had two API mismatches.
   - Fix: edited `main.js` to match the real `Input` / bootstrap APIs.

     - `three/addons/postprocessing/RenderPass.js`
     - `three/addons/postprocessing/UnrealBloomPass.js`
     - `three/addons/postprocessing/OutputPass.js`

Let me record one more lesson about the Input edge-detection bug, since it's a subtle one that cost time.

Input.update() must NOT clear the edge-press set (_pressed) at the top of the frame — keyboard keydown events fire between frames and add edges that the game reads via pressed() later in the same frame. Clearing _pressed in update() wipes fast key presses (down+up within one frame), so pause/start toggles silently fail. Compute edges as the set-difference of held-now vs held-last-frame instead.

## What I reconciled and fixed

The hand-off flagged API mismatches in `Game.js`, but the real problems were broader. After reading every file and building the exact API map, I fixed:

**Bootstrap (`main.js` / `index.html`)**
- `getElementById('game-root')` → `#app` (the actual container)
- `new Arena(scene)` → `new Arena(scene, textures)` — Arena requires a `ProceduralTextures` instance
- `new Game({ engine, … })` → `new Game({ scene, … })` — Game reads `scene`, not `engine`
- Removed the dead `fx.trail` (Bullets build their own trails) and added the missing `arena.update(realDt)` (starfield + light-flash decay were never running)
- Rewrote `index.html`: the static HUD/screens used CSS class names that didn't match UI.js's generated markup at all, and the duplicate `id="hud"` broke the UI root. Now the CSS matches UI.js exactly and the dead static DOM is gone.

**Game logic (`Game.js`)**
- Menu never showed on load — constructor set `state='menu'` but never called `_setState('menu')`
- SHIELD power-up was dead — `player.hit()` (the shield absorb) was never called
- UFO never appeared — `ufo.launch()` was never triggered; added a per-wave spawn timer
- Victory state was unreachable — `MAX_WAVE` was defined but unused; wired the wave-10 → victory path

**Entity bugs**
- `Bullets.js` called `trail.reset()` — `MotionTrail` has `clear()`, not `reset()` (threw on every shot)
- `PowerUp.testCollect` returned a pickup whose type had already been reset to `'RAPID'` by the pool's release hook — so a BOMB pickup applied RAPID. Now snapshots fields before release.
- `Player.wide` was never initialized in the constructor

**Shared (`Input.js`)**
- `update()` cleared the edge-press set every frame, wiping keyboard presses that fired between frames — fast pause/start toggles silently failed. Now edges are computed as held-now vs held-last-frame.

## What I verified (real Chrome, zero runtime errors)
- Menu → LAUNCH → playing; HUD score/wave/lives correct
- Fire, move, pause/resume all work
- **Loss path**: 3 deaths → "EARTH FALLEN" game-over → RETRY restarts (reached in ~14s of real play)
- **Win path**: wave-10 clear → "GALAXY SECURED" victory → PLAY AGAIN resets to wave 1
- BOMB clears enemy bullets; SHIELD sets `player.shield`; UFO kill scores + deactivates
- Production build (`vite preview`) loads and plays identically
- `vite build` clean (39 modules), no unresolved imports, no missing methods, no stubs/placeholders

Two footguns I hit are recorded in workspace memory (the pool-reset-mutates-item trap and the Input edge-clearing bug) so they don't cost the next agent time.
